title: TAS: BusinessReady, vehicle registration and VesselReady (licences, insurance, tax, trades, personal services, childcare, imported vehicles, boats)
notes: First sourced Tasmanian rules for BusinessReady, TradeReady (vehicles) and VesselReady. Built from Department of Health, City of Hobart, Liquor and Gaming Branch, WorkSafe Tasmania, State Revenue Office, CBOS (now Consumer Affairs Tasmania and Building Standards Tasmania, from 1 October 2026), Transport Tasmania, Service Tasmania and MAST pages, ABLIS entries and the Occupational Licensing (Building Services Work) Regulations 2016, read on 2026-10-12. No Tasmanian Government business grant was confirmed open or recurring for 2026 (the Accelerating Trade Grant Program was closed with no 2026-27 round announced), so there are no GrantReady rule sets. Every reference is UNVERIFIED and carries a summary, not the source's wording: staff must capture each source, replace the extract with the exact text and verify it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] The City of Hobart says food premises must be registered by the local council under the Food Act 2003. One online food business application is used for notification, registration and taking over an existing business. For a first registration an Environmental Health Officer inspects the premises before the certificate of registration is issued, and the certificate is needed before opening. Annual fees and inspection frequency depend on the risk class (low, medium or high); registrations expire on 31 May each year and the council sends a renewal form. Certain businesses may need a food safety supervisor under the national Food Safety Standard. Mobile food trucks also need a licence.

rule_sets.title: Tasmania: business licences, insurance and tax
rule_sets.description: Registrations, licences, insurance and tax most Tasmanian businesses check: food business registration with council, food safety supervisors, liquor licences, outdoor dining permits, workers compensation insurance and payroll tax.
limitations: Built from Department of Health, City of Hobart, Department of Treasury and Finance, WorkSafe Tasmania and State Revenue Office pages, not from the Acts themselves.
Council details (forms, fees, renewal dates) come from the City of Hobart as an example. Other Tasmanian councils run the same registrations with their own forms and fees.
Does not decide which liquor licence you need. We use the on-licence operating as a restaurant as the example; bars, bottle shops and clubs use other licence types.
Does not check planning approval for the use of your premises or a fit-out.
Not legal or tax advice. Confirm with the regulator or a qualified professional before you rely on it.

outcomes.title: Register your food business with your council before you open
outcomes.detail: Under the Food Act 2003 (Tas), food premises must be registered by the local council. Apply to your council's environmental health team before you open: for a first registration an Environmental Health Officer inspects the premises before issuing the certificate of registration, and you need the certificate before you trade. Annual fees depend on your risk class (low, medium or high). In Hobart, registrations expire on 31 May each year and the council sends a renewal form. Food vans also need registration.

rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Appoint a certified food safety supervisor and train your food handlers
outcomes.detail: The national Food Safety Standard 3.2.2A applies in Tasmania. Cafes, restaurants, takeaways, caterers and food vans that handle unpackaged, potentially hazardous food must appoint a certified food safety supervisor, and food handlers must be trained. Your council's Environmental Health Officer checks this. The Department of Health lists food safety supervisor courses, and its DoFoodSafely course is free.

rules.title: Liquor licence
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: You need a Tasmanian liquor licence from the Commissioner for Licensing
outcomes.detail: Selling alcohol in Tasmania needs a licence from the Commissioner for Licensing, through the Liquor and Gaming Branch of the Department of Treasury and Finance. Fill in the Tasmanian Liquor Licence Application Form and email it to licensing@treasury.tas.gov.au with plans showing the licensed area in red, council planning approval to sell liquor at the premises, your RSA certificate, ID, a business plan, proof of tenure, photos and a menu. You must advertise in a local newspaper and at the premises; people then have 14 days to support or object. A complete application takes about 4 to 6 weeks. An on-licence for a restaurant costs $784 to apply and $509.60 a year.

rules.title: Payroll tax
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Check whether you must register for Tasmanian payroll tax
outcomes.detail: Tasmanian payroll tax applies once your total Australian taxable wages (including grouped businesses) pass $1.25 million a year and you pay wages in Tasmania. For 2026-27 the rate is 4% on wages between $1.25 million and $2 million, and 6.1% above $2 million. Register with the State Revenue Office once you pass the threshold. With 20 or more staff you may be near it.

outcomes.detail: In Tasmania anyone who performs building work, other than low-risk work under the Building Act 2016, must hold a building services provider licence as a builder under the Occupational Licensing Act 2005. rules.title: Residential building work contracts
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Use a written contract for home building jobs of $20,000 or more
outcomes.detail: Under the Residential Building Work Contracts and Dispute Resolution Act 2016, residential building work with a contract price of $20,000 or more needs a written, dated contract signed by you and the owner. It must include your licence number, a clear description of the work with plans and specifications, the price and how it's worked out, the completion date and the statutory warranties. Give the owner a signed copy and the CBOS residential building consumer guide within 5 business days. The owner can cool off within 5 business days. Deposits are capped at 10% for contracts from $20,000 to $50,000 and 5% for $50,000 or more, and you can't ask for more than 50% of the price until half the work is done.

rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Get the vehicle inspected at an Approved Inspection Station, then register it at Service Tasmania
outcomes.detail: Book an inspection directly with an Approved Inspection Station (AIS) and take your Vehicle Import Approval (or concessional RAV entry approval). If the vehicle passes, complete the registration application on the back of the passed inspection report. Vehicles with no Australian registration history may first need to be entered on the Register of Approved Vehicles. Then take the report, the import approval, proof of entitlement and your Tasmanian driver licence or ID to a Service Tasmania centre. You pay the registration fee (a 4-cylinder car is $669.23 to establish in 2026-27, including plates), the MAIB premium ($305 for a car) and motor vehicle duty: $3 for every $100 of value, or 4% for passenger vehicles over $40,000. Left-hand drive vehicles must be at least 30 years old.

outcomes.title: Register the boat with MAST
outcomes.detail: In Tasmania, recreational boats with a motor of 4 horsepower or more, and all personal watercraft (jet skis), must be registered with MAST before use. You must be 16 or older. Fill in the MAST Application for Registration of a Recreational Vessel and lodge it with evidence of identity and proof of ownership, at MAST or a Service Tasmania centre. Registration costs $95.50 a year (to 31 December 2026) and renews each 31 December. MAST mails your certificate. Display the numbers on each side: at least 150 mm high on a planing boat, 75 mm on a non-planing boat or PWC.

The licence lasts up to three years: all licences currently expire on 30 June 2027 and the fee is worked out pro rata to that date. People aged 12 to 17 can get a provisional licence. Interstate licence holders can operate for up to 3 months; to transfer, lodge the MAST Application for Mutual Recognition of a Motor Boat Licence.
